id: -2400-盧加爾-安尼-蒙杜對烏爾的行動
theater: 美索不達米亞南部阿達布與烏爾

battle.name: 盧加爾-安尼-蒙杜對烏爾的行動
battle.theater: 美索不達米亞南部阿達布與烏爾
battle.brief: 約公元前2365年，河間城邦阿達布的國王盧加爾-安尼-蒙杜集結市民軍隊南下，攻滅由南尼之子梅什卡利安納納統治的烏爾城邦，把「王權」從烏爾帶到阿達布，蘇美爾史上第一次出現城邦王權的整體轉移。卡面是早王朝時期的埃及長矛，屬同期的青銅長柄刺器，與本役同時流行於近東各地。

kit.name: 埃及長矛
kit.history: 早王朝時期的長矛，銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上。埃及人用它守城垣，後來也用它收復失地。

countries: 這場戰爭是公元前二十五世紀末蘇美爾城邦之間爭奪「王權」的一次武力衝突，發生在美索不達米亞南部的幼發拉底河兩岸：一方是內陸城邦阿達布，另一方是海運發達的烏爾城邦。阿達布位於尼普爾東南約三十五公里的俾斯馬亞，靠近從幼發拉底分出的一條主渠道，耕地平整而灌溉穩定；烏爾則坐落在幼發拉底與埃伊克福之間的南部沖積平原，扼住通往波斯灣的碼頭，是當時最富的城之一。交戰雙方都不是常備軍國家：阿達布由國王盧加爾-安尼-蒙杜以王權直接統率的市民徵召兵為主，兵源是城內由王室供裝備的農民戶與專職戰士；烏爾方面則由王族南尼一系的家族成員領銜，號召城民與附庸城邑的民兵守衛王城與神域。環繞兩家的第三方勢力同樣關鍵：北方的馬里城邦沿幼發拉底上行，把阿達布夾在腹地；拉格什與烏馬在南部互相攻伐，都想趁烏爾衰敗奪取王權；更東面是埃蘭與古提姆等山地強勢，北方還有敘利亞與阿馬爾的商旅與掠奪者。蘇美爾的王權長期繫於尼普爾的「王權」觀念，此役卻把這個名號從烏爾整體搬到阿達布，是已知最早的一次城邦霸權整體轉移。
countriesEn: This war was an armed clash between Sumerian city-states over the prize of kingship in the late twenty-fifth century BC, fought on both banks of the lower Euphrates in southern Mesopotamia: on one side the inland city of Adab, on the other the maritime city of Ur. Adab lay about thirty-five kilometres southeast of Nippur at modern Bismaya, close to one of the main canals that branches off the Euphrates, with level fields and a stable irrigation network. Ur sat on the southern alluvial plain between the Euphrates and the Eiak, commanding the quays that led towards the Persian Gulf, and was already one of the richest cities of the age. Neither side was a state with a standing army. Adab's host was a citizen levy under the direct command of King Lugal-Anne-Mundu, drawing on peasant households that the palace equipped, together with a body of full-time warriors attached to the crown. Ur's side was led by members of the royal house of Nanni, rallying the city's armed men and the militias of dependent towns to defend the royal quarter and the sanctuaries. The third parties around them mattered just as much: Mari was pushing up the Euphrates from the north, squeezing Adab from behind; Lagash and Umma were tearing each other apart in the south, both eager to pick up whatever Ur was dropping; further east lay Elam and Gutium, and to the north the traders and raiders of Syria and Amurru. Sumerian kingship was long bound to the concept of the kingship of Nippur, yet this war moved that title from Ur to Adab entire, the earliest known wholesale transfer of a city-state hegemony.
people: 核心人物是阿達布王盧加爾-安尼-蒙杜，楔形文字作盧加爾-阿內-穆恩杜，號「四方之王」，《蘇美爾王表》列他是阿達布王朝唯一一位國王，統治九十年（此數字本身可能有誤）。他不只是戰場上的統帥，銘文裡自稱「供養尼普爾的強者」，把伊南圖這位國母女神與恩利爾的祭司地位一併置於自己的庇護之下，顯示他要爭的從來不只是地盤，而是王權的名分。被他從王位上打落的是烏爾王室的南尼及其子梅什卡利安納納；後者在位時烏爾正被拉格什的恩納圖姆父子壓制，一場敗仗之後，烏爾的霸權出現真空，阿達布的軍隊才得以南下接替。傳世後來的那篇「盧加爾-安尼-蒙杜銘文」還提到由馬爾哈希的恩西米吉爾恩利爾率領、名字多為閃米特式的十三位叛亂首領，逐一被請上金座，這批名字說明阿達布的對手陣營裡塞著大量阿姆爾特人首領。學者方面，1909年波貝爾首次整理銘文殘片，1934年古特博克判定它屬偽托，現代研究（弗賴恩《前薩爾貢時期》）則傾向把它看作古巴比倫時代的文學虛構；因此本役的細節多靠《蘇美爾王表》一句「烏爾以武力被擊倒」撐住。
peopleEn: The central figure is Lugal-Anne-Mundu, king of Adab, written Lugal-an-ne₂-mu-un-du₃ and titled king of the four quarters. The Sumerian King List makes him the only ruler of the dynasty of Adab and credits him with ninety years of rule, though that figure is damaged and doubted. He was not merely a commander in the field: in his inscription he calls himself the strong man who provides for Nippur and places the office of the queen of temples, the mother of the land Nintu, together with the standing of Enlil under his protection, which shows that what he was after was never only territory but the name of kingship itself. The rulers he unseated belonged to the house of Nanni of Ur, namely Nanni and his son Mesh-kali-ang-Nanna; the latter had himself been pressed by Enannatum and Enmetena of Lagash, and a defeat at Uruk had opened a gap in Ur's hegemony through which the army of Adab marched south. The later text known as the Lugal-Anne-Mundu inscription also names a coalition of thirteen rebel governors and chiefs led by Migir-Enlil, ensi of Marhashi, whose names are largely Semitic; these names show that the opposing camp was packed with Amorite leaders. On the scholarly side, Arno Poebel published a first reading of the fragments in 1909, Hans Gustav Güterbock dismissed the text as pseudepigraphic in 1934, and modern work such as Frayne's Presargonic Period treats it as a literary fiction of the Old Babylonian period. The detail of this war therefore rests on a single line of the Sumerian King List: Ur was struck down with weapons.
kits: 卡面這件埃及長矛屬青銅時代的早期長柄刺器，銅或青銅矛頭以繩纏綁在木杆上，是近東各地共通的步兵裝備；同時代的埃及人用它在城垣上防守，也用它向外收復失地。蘇美爾這邊的兵器譜系與之相去不遠：矛頭多為中空套接式的銅器，長矛與短矛並行，弓手配骨或燧石箭頭，另有銅斧、匕首、石鏃、投石索與木框蒙皮的盾牌。烏爾「王家墓地」出土的「烏爾軍旗」戰爭一側畫著四輪戰車與持矛護衛，說明車兵在烏爾第一王朝末年已存在，但這次遠征的實際戰鬥仍以步兵為主。攻城一方需要撞木、繩梯、填壕的土袋與臨時工事，防守一方則依靠城牆、塔樓與唯一的主門。補給靠河：阿達布至烏爾約一百一十至一百五十公里，沿幼發拉底與其支渠航行，軍糧從阿達布周邊的田地徵發，銅料則靠馬里與埃蘭方向的交換取得。真正稀少的是鐵：整場戰爭的兵器全部是銅、燧石、骨與木，沒有一件鐵器。
kitsEn: The card's Egyptian spear is an early bronze-age long thrusting weapon, a copper or bronze blade bound with cord to a wooden shaft, and it was the common infantry arm across the Near East; the Egyptians of the Old Kingdom used it on the city wall and again when recovering lost ground. The Sumerian armory stood close to this: socketed copper spearheads with a hollow tang, long and short spears used side by side, bows with bone or flint arrowheads, plus copper axes, daggers, flint blades, slings and wooden frames covered with hide. The war side of the Standard of Ur, recovered in the royal cemetery of Ur, shows four-wheeled war wagons and spear-bearing guards, so wheeled vehicles already existed in Ur at the end of the first dynasty, though the foot soldier remained the core of any such campaign. The besieger needed beams for battering, ladders, sacks of earth for filling ditches and improvised works; the defenders relied on the city wall, its towers and the single main gate. Supply came by river: Adab and Ur are roughly one hundred and ten to one hundred and fifty kilometres apart, and the army moved down the Euphrates and its branches, with grain requisitioned from the fields around Adab and copper obtained through exchange with Mari and Elam. What was genuinely scarce was iron. Not one iron object appears in the armament of this war; everything was copper, flint, bone and wood.
tactics: 關於戰術，現代學者可確定的有限，只能從蘇美爾人的作戰習慣與《蘇美爾王表》的措辭推敲。王表寫「烏爾以武力被擊倒，王權被帶到阿達布」，用詞與同表其他王朝更替完全一致，說明這不是和平禪讓，而是有實戰的攻伐。一般認為阿達布軍隊沿幼發拉底支渠南下，先在開闢的耕地一線集結，徵召城內持矛弓的農民兵與王室依附的專職戰士，兵員以步兵為主，輔以少量乘驢或乘牛的運輸與偵察人員，糧秣靠船隻沿河輸送而非靠車輛。面對烏爾的城牆，遠征軍最可能採取的是圍城與強攻並用：先以弓手壓制城頭，再以撞木與梯隊攻擊主門，破城之後控制神廟區與碼頭，奪取王室的穀物、銅料與對外貿易的船隊。城破之後如何收編原有王權象徵、把尼普爾的「王權」帶回阿達布，靠的是儀式與神廟捐獻，而不是長期駐紮。文中多處提到「金座」，說明勝利者用奪來的財富與器物收買盟邦與首領的忠誠，這是當時城邦聯盟維持秩序的基本手段。戰術細節之所以難以落實，是因為唯一的同期材料只有那篇被判定為文學虛構的後世銘文。
tacticsEn: On tactics, modern scholars can establish very little and must work from Sumerian practice and the wording of the King List. The list says that Ur was struck down with weapons and that the kingship was carried off to Adab, a formula identical to the one used for every other dynastic turnover in the same list, which tells us this was not a peaceful abdication but a war. In general it is thought that the Adab host moved south along the branches of the Euphrates, mustered on the already cleared farmland, drew in the townsmen armed with spear and bow, and put the crown's full-time warriors in the van, with infantry forming the bulk and a small number of donkey and ox drivers serving as transport and scouts, provisions travelling by boat rather than cart. Facing the walls of Ur, the expedition most likely combined siege and assault: archers to pin the wall, then battering beams and ladder teams against the main gate, and once the city fell, control of the temple quarter and the quays, seizing grain, copper and the merchant fleets. How the victory was then turned into legitimate authority, carrying the kingship of Nippur back to Adab, depended on ritual and temple donation rather than on a long garrison. The text speaks again and again of golden thrones, which shows that the conqueror used captured wealth to buy the loyalty of allies and chiefs, the basic instrument by which Sumerian city leagues were held together. The reason tactical detail cannot be firmed up is that the only period source is the later inscription judged to be a literary fiction.
data: 可核對的數字極少，而且多為後世清單的殘值。《蘇美爾王表》記阿達布的盧加爾-安尼-蒙杜統治九十年，但清單本身有殘缺，現代學者多不採信此數，改以城邦阿達布短暫崛起又迅速崩落推算，落在公元前2500至2400年之間。戰爭年表把本役定在公元前2365年前後，與烏爾第一王朝末年、拉格什與烏馬爭奪南部控制權的年代重疊。地理數字較可靠：阿達布在尼普爾東南約三十五公里，烏爾在幼發拉底下游南岸，兩城直線距離約一百一十公里，沿河行軍要一百一十至一百五十公里。銘文提到十三位叛亂首領，以及雪松山、埃蘭、馬爾哈希、古提姆、蘇巴爾圖、阿馬爾、西提烏姆等七八個被征服或進貢的地區，數目遠大於同期任何一份可比對的名單。烏爾王家墓地在同一時期封閉，歷代王室的陪葬集中在前王朝末段的一段短時間內，僅存的高等級王墓即達十六座級別，說明烏爾一度極盛而衰落極快。本戰役的確切月份無文獻可考，卡面取四月，是按兩河流域春汛退水、田事方興的傳統出征時令安排的。
dataEn: Very few figures can be checked, and most of them are damaged values in later lists. The Sumerian King List gives Lugal-Anne-Mundu ninety years of rule over Adab, but the list is broken at that point and scholars generally distrust the figure, dating the brief ascendancy of Adab instead between roughly 2500 and 2400 BC on the strength of the city's rapid rise and equally rapid collapse. The chronology of wars places this campaign around 2365 BC, overlapping the end of the first dynasty of Ur and the struggle between Lagash and Umma for control of the southern cities. The geographical figures are firmer: Adab lay some thirty-five kilometres southeast of Nippur, Ur lay on the south bank of the lower Euphrates, and the straight-line distance between them is about one hundred and ten kilometres, one hundred and ten to one hundred and fifty by the river route. The inscription names thirteen rebel chiefs and seven or eight regions brought under tribute or submission, among them the Cedar Mountain, Elam, Marhashi, Gutium, Subartu, Amurru and Sutium, a reach far beyond anything that can be matched in a contemporary list. The royal cemetery of Ur was sealed at the same time, the burials of successive rulers crowded into a short stretch of the late Early Dynastic period, sixteen royal tombs of the first rank, sealing away both the wealth of Ur and its decline. The exact month of the war is recorded nowhere; the card's month of April follows the traditional campaigning season of the Euphrates valley, after the spring flood had subsided and the fields were being worked.
cause: 動因有三層。第一層是王權之爭：蘇美爾各城邦並不共享一個國家，而是各據一城、各有城邦之王，爭的是「四方之王」這個名號所帶來的護城河、小麥、勞役與神廟地位。烏爾第一王朝靠海運、香柏木與南部城邑的進貢登上王位，其內陸的北界卻正撞上拉格什的恩納圖姆父子；恩梅塔納在烏克一役打敗南尼之子梅什卡利安納納之後，烏爾的霸權裂開一道口子。第二層是阿達布自身的上升動能：它離尼普爾近、土地肥沃、灌溉渠道密集，國王又是城邦中少數能用「四方之王」自號者，奪取王權既有利於控制神廟與商路，也有正當性可講。第三層是區域格局的整體鬆動：北部馬里的阿姆爾特人南下、東部埃蘭與古提姆的山地勢力西壓、南部拉格什與烏馬互鬥消耗，加上遠方商路中斷，烏爾用來維持霸權的資源基礎被抽走。三層壓力疊在一起，烏爾在軍事上孤立，阿達布的出征才有可能成功。
causeEn: There are three layers of motive. The first is the struggle for kingship: the Sumerian cities did not share a state, each held one city with its own city king, and what they contended for was the title of king of the four quarters together with what it carried, the dikes, the barley, the labour levy and the standing of the temples. The first dynasty of Ur had risen on maritime trade, cedar and the tribute of the southern towns, and its inland northern frontier ran straight into Lagash and Enannatum; when Enmetena defeated Mesh-kali-ang-Nanna, son of Nanni, at Uruk, a crack opened in Ur's hegemony. The second is Adab's own rising momentum: close to Nippur, with fertile land and dense canals, ruled by one of the few rulers of the age who dared call himself king of the four quarters, seizing the kingship would bring control of the temples and the trade routes as well as the name. The third is the general loosening of the regional order: Amorite pressure from Mari in the north, Elamite and Gutian mountain powers pressing from the east, Lagash and Umma wearing each other down in the south, and the breakdown of distant trade routes, all of it draining the resource base that had kept Ur dominant. The three pressures together left Ur militarily isolated, and only then could the expedition from Adab succeed.
impact: 此役的直接影響，是蘇美爾的權力中心第一次整體位移。烏爾不再坐在王座上，「王權」落到內陸的阿達布，說明王權是可以被搬走的物件，誰能控制尼普爾周邊的軍力與神廟，誰就能繼承它。第二是烏爾王室的終結：王家墓地在烏爾第一王朝末年封閉，密集下葬的陪葬品把這座城最富的年代封存，同時把衰敗也一併封存，烏爾此後數百年只是眾城之一。第三是阿達布的短命：國王死後帝國瓦解，《蘇美爾王表》說「阿達布以武力被擊倒，王權被帶到馬里」，但多數學者認為真正握有霸權的只是馬里的沙魯米特一人，而拉格什的盧加蘭達、艾克沙克的普祖爾尼拉與烏馬的盧加爾扎格西各自建國，說明那不是一次改朝換姓，而是蘇美爾整體碎裂。於是「有記錄歷史上的第一個帝國」在建立者死後即告瓦解，此後幾百年，兩河流域由城邦競逐主導，直到烏爾第三王朝才重新整合南部。
impactEn: The immediate effect was the first complete shift of the centre of power in Sumer. Ur no longer sat on the throne and the kingship passed inland to Adab, showing that kingship was a transferable object: whoever could hold the military force and the temples around Nippur could inherit it. Second, the Ur dynasty was over. The royal cemetery was sealed at the end of the first dynasty, its dense concentration of grave goods preserving the richest age of the city and, with it, its decline, and for centuries afterwards Ur was one city among many. Third, Adab's empire was short-lived. On the king's death it fell apart, and the King List says that Adab was struck down with weapons and the kingship carried off to Mari, but most scholars hold that only Sharrumiter of Mari actually exercised that hegemony, while Lugalanda of Lagash, Puzur-Nirah of Akshak and Lugal-zage-si of Umma each founded their own state. What happened, in other words, was not a change of dynasty but the fragmentation of Sumer as a whole. The first empire in recorded history thus dissolved as soon as its founder died, and the cities of the Euphrates went on competing as independent polities for centuries, until the third dynasty of Ur reassembled the south.
result: 「烏爾以武力被擊倒，王權被帶到阿達布」，這句《蘇美爾王表》的總結至今仍是最可靠的戰果陳述：梅什卡利安納納一系的烏爾王統治終結，烏爾城與其王位被阿達布接收，尼普爾方向的王權轉入盧加爾-安尼-蒙杜之手。就戰役本身而言，能確定的是一場以武力解決的城邦兼併，以及隨之而來的王室財富與對外航線的轉手；不能確定的是攻城方式、兵力規模與損失數字，因為同期材料幾乎全缺，唯一的細節來源那篇後世銘文已被判為文學虛構。戰役之後阿達布並未長期守住成果：國王一死，其帝國隨即分崩，王權在名目上轉到馬里，實則由拉格什、艾克沙克、烏馬各霸一方，蘇美爾進入城邦林立的分裂期。烏爾則要到不到三百年後，由第三王朝的烏爾納姆穆重建王號，才重新成為兩河流域南部的中心城之一。
resultEn: Ur was struck down with weapons and the kingship was carried off to Adab: that sentence from the Sumerian King List remains the most reliable statement of the outcome. The Ur dynasty of Mesh-kali-ang-Nanna came to an end, the city of Ur and its throne passed to Adab, and the kingship of the Nippur direction came into the hands of Lugal-Anne-Mundu. What can be established about the war itself is an armed annexation of one city-state by another, and the consequent transfer of royal wealth and of the outward shipping lines. What cannot be established is the method of the assault, the size of the armies and the losses, because period material is almost entirely lacking and the only detailed source, the later inscription, has been judged a literary fiction. The campaign bought Adab no lasting result: on the king's death the empire dissolved, the kingship passed in name to Mari, and in practice Lagash, Akshak and Umma each held its own part, leaving Sumer in a period of competing city-states. Ur was not to return as a centre of the southern riverlands until a little under three centuries later, when Ur-Nammu of the third dynasty rebuilt the royal title at Ur.
